title: Dynamic prefetch validation and safe unwind policy for cost-driven batching/caching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We have multiple autotune recommendations that enable more aggressive prefix prefetching and dynamic microbatch aggregation to reduce per-token cost. Prior tickets focused on instrumentation and sentinel tests for simple cache/batch toggles, but customers with long-turn dialogue flows or legal/regulatory text have shown non-linear quality regressions when prefetch heuristics change. This ticket implements validation for a new Dynamic Prefetcher (heuristics that vary cache TTL and prefetch depth by customer/request entropy) and a conservative, automated unwind (safe rollback) policy if quality regressions are detected.

Goal: Provide an end-to-end acceptance path that ties cost-saving config changes to measurable quality constraints: 1) automated stratified evaluation (by request shape, length, and customer tier); 2) embedding-based semantic drift detection against a persisted golden corpus; 3) statistically-powered equivalence testing with pre-specified deltas; 4) automated gradual unwind policy that can revert or throttle changes without human-in-the-loop when regression thresholds are exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: A1: The validation harness runs a stratified eval across at least 10k requests (sampled across short/long/interactive flows) and produces per-stratum deltas for token-level latency, cost, and two semantic metrics: embedding cosine delta and semantic BLEU-like score.

A2: Semantic regression is flagged if embedding cosine similarity to golden outputs drops below 0.92 (per-stratum median) AND a paired TOST equivalence test fails with delta=0.03 for the semantic score (alpha=0.05).

A3: If regression is triggered, the system enters a staged unwind: first reduce prefetch depth by 50% for 30 minutes, then fall back to previous config if no improvement; these steps must be automated and visible in Console with runbook links.
A4: The system produces an audit artifact (S3 path) with sample diffs, top-50 highest-delta requests, and human-review tags; human reviewer can certify fix and re-enable full autotune.

A5: Dashboards (Datadog + Console) show cost delta, latency P50/P95, semantic-drift index, and a binary safety flag. No rollout passes to GA without safety flag cleared for 72 hours on canary traffic.
A6: Unit/integration tests covering the shadow-apply path, synthetic golden corpus replay, and the unwind automation are present and in CI.
test_plan: 1) Shadow-apply: run Dynamic Prefetcher config in shadow on 10% of incoming traffic for 48h; collect metrics and compute stratified deltas. 2) Replay-benchmark: replay stored production traces (~10k traces) against baseline and candidate configs, compute embedding and token-level metrics. 3) Human audit: pull top 200 regressions into the audit UI for two reviewers. 4) Equivalence testing: run paired TOST on semantic scores per stratum. 5) Canary: 1% traffic with full apply and unwind automation active; must pass 72h stability window to expand.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Local dev + unit tests. Phase 1: Shadow-apply on non-prod traces. Phase 2: Replay-benchmark on persisted trace corpus. Phase 3: Canary (1% traffic, automatic unwind enabled). Phase 4: Gradual ramp (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) only if no safety flag triggers and human-review sign-off after 72h on each step. Unwind steps are automated with exponential backoff and an immediate emergency revert endpoint. All steps logged to audit S3 and Console.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Semantic regressions not caught by token-level metrics. Mitigation: embedding-based semantic delta + human audit for top diffs.
Risk: Insufficient sample size for rare flows (legal docs, code). Mitigation: stratified sampling with oversampling of low-frequency request shapes and customer-provided golden prompts.
Risk: Automated unwind loops too aggressive and oscillate config. Mitigation: add cooldown window (30m) and exponential backoff multiplier before re-applying a change.
Risk: Cost savings incentivize pushing heuristics too far. Mitigation: hard safety guard that requires semantic equivalence test pass before any >10% prefetch increase on enterprise customers.
decisions: Use embedding-cosine (Ada-002 embeddings) as primary semantic signal (decision 2025-02-14).
Adopt paired TOST (two-one-sided t-test) with delta=0.03 for semantic score equivalence instead of raw BLEU thresholds (decision 2025-02-18).
Automated unwind will be staged (throttle -> partial revert -> full revert) with 30m cooldowns between steps (decision 2025-02-20).
